prompt: In a theatre, row $1$ has $12$ seats. Every row after that has $3$ more seats than the row in front of it. How many seats are in row $20$?
hint: The same amount is added each row, so this is an ARITHMETIC sequence with $a_1 = 12$ and $d = 3$.

hints.text: The same amount is added each row, so this is an ARITHMETIC sequence with $a_1 = 12$ and $d = 3$.
Row $20$ is $19$ rows behind row $1$, so it has gained $19$ jumps of $3$ seats, which is $57$ extra seats. Add those to row 1.
Adding gives $12 + 57 = 69$, so row $20$ has $69$ seats.

explanation: The rows follow $a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d$ with first term $a_1 = 12$ and common difference $d = 3$.
For row $20$ the formula gives the seat count $a_{20} = 12 + (20 - 1) \times 3$.
Multiplying first, this is the same as $12 + 19 \times 3 = 12 + 57$.
So row $20$ of the theatre has $69$ seats.

alternativeExplanations.title: A short table, then a leap
steps: Look at row 4: it is 12 + 3(3), and the 3 is one less than the row number.
So row 20 is 12 + 19(3) = 69. The table finds the pattern; the formula does the leap.

alternativeExplanations.title: Work backwards to check
steps: If row 20 really holds 69 seats, walk backwards 19 rows of 3.
That is exactly row 1, so the answer checks out.
